name: Alfa Romeo
overview: The passionate Italian driver's marque, renowned in Australia for melodic twin-cam engines, Bathurst class victories, and the Giorgio-platform Giulia and Stelvio.
australian_history: Alfa Romeo established strong Australian presence in the 1960s with distributor Alec Mildren, whose racing team campaigned Giulia and GTA models with immense success. At the Bathurst 500, Alfa Romeo GT and 1750 GTVs won their classes repeatedly. The 105 Series Giulia, Bertone Coupe (1750/2000 GTV), and Spider Veloce became Australian motoring royalty. Transaxle models like the Alfetta, GTV6, and 75 followed in the 1970s and 1980s. Modern Alfa Romeo is represented by the 156, 147, 159, and the celebrated rear-wheel-drive Giorgio platform: the Giulia sports sedan and Stelvio SUV, crowned by 375kW Ferrari-developed 2.9L twin-turbo V6 Quadrifoglio models.

giulia-gtv.name: Giulia Sprint GT, GTV & Giulia Quadrifoglio
giulia-gtv.overview: The passionate soul of Italian motoring in Australia. Spanning from the Bertone-styled 105 Series Giulia Sprint GT and Bathurst-winning 1750/2000 GTV, through the transaxle Alfetta GTV6 Group A touring car, to the spine-tingling Busso V6 156 GTA and the modern Giorgio-platform Giulia Quadrifoglio with its Ferrari-derived 375kW twin-turbo V6.
giulia-gtv.australian_market_notes: First sold in Australia in 1964 (105 Series Giulia Sprint GT). The 105 GTV scored class wins in the Armstrong 500 at Bathurst. In the 1980s, Colin Bond and Alan Jones campaigned the howling Alfetta GTV6 in the Australian Touring Car Championship. The 952 Giulia Quadrifoglio set a production sedan benchmark at Mount Panorama.

generations.summary: Masterpiece designed by Giorgetto Giugiaro for Bertone. Featured all-alloy twin-cam four-cylinder engines, twin Weber/Dell'Orto carburettors, 5-speed manual, four-wheel disc brakes, and Bathurst 500 class dominance.
